title: A young gas giant and hidden substructures in a protoplanetary disk
question: Does the apparently structureless disk of MP Mus hide substructures at 3 mm, and can a companion in the inner disk explain both the Gaia proper motion anomaly and the 3 mm cavity?

recipe.goal: Calibrate and self-calibrate ALMA Band 3 and Band 6 data
recipe.method: Pipeline calibration, then phase-only self-calibration per configuration, re-centring, flux rescaling between executions and a final combined self-cal round
key_parameters: CASA 6.4.1.12 pipeline then 6.5.6.22 (Band 3); CASA 5.1.1-5 pipeline then 6.5.6.22 (Band 6)

recipe.goal: Image the continuum at 1.3 and 3 mm
recipe.method: tclean with mtmfs, nterms=1, multiscale 0,1,3,5 beams, robust = 0 for both bands
key_parameters: rms 37 uJy/beam (1.3 mm) and 7.7 uJy/beam (3 mm); peak S/N 105 and 90

recipe.method: FRANK fit of the axisymmetric profile from visibilities (Hankel transform), geometry fitted non-parametrically first
key_parameters: 3 mm: alpha = 1.3, w_smooth = 1e-2 (lower values gave artificial ripples)

recipe.goal: Check substructures are not FRANK artefacts
recipe.method: Radial profiles from robust=-0.5 tclean images with GOFISH, and a GPUVMEM image with no entropy term (positivity only)

recipe.goal: Measure 3 mm flux, dust mass and disk radii
recipe.method: Flux from robust=0.5 image; dust mass from optically thin emission with bootstrap over flux, temperature and beta; radii from the cumulative intensity profile of robust=0 images
key_parameters: Dust temperature 20 K (Normal, sigma 2.5 K in bootstrap); beta uniform 0 to 0.5; 1000 bootstrap draws; median and 16/84 percentiles reported
assumptions: Optically thin emission, average dust temperature 20 K, power-law dust opacity; gas-to-dust ratio 100 used later for disk mass in simulations

recipe.goal: Constrain companion mass and separation from the Gaia proper motion anomaly
recipe.method: Compare Gaia DR2 and DR3 proper motions, then simulate Gaia observations of a two-body system with 500 000 random draws and keep those matching the observed anomaly and RUWE
key_parameters: Mass ratio 0.0001 to 1 and period 0.016 to 1585 yr, log-uniform; selection UWE_DR3 < 1.1; stellar mass 1.30 +/- 0.08 Msun, inclination 32 +/- 1 deg, PA 10 +/- 1 deg
assumptions: No eccentricity; light ratio l = q^3.5; PMa dominated by a single companion

recipe.goal: Run SPH hydrodynamic models of a star plus planet in the disk
recipe.method: Grid of 25 3D PHANTOM simulations, one-fluid dust with five grain sizes, evolved for 1000 planet orbits
key_parameters: N = 1e6 particles; R_out = 50 au; R_in = 1.5 a_p; alpha_AV = 0.2, beta_AV = 2 (alpha_ss = 5e-3); disk mass 0.01 Msun; star 1.3 Msun; H/R = 0.1 at 100 au; grains 1 um to 0.5 cm, n(s) proportional to s^-3.5, 3 g/cm3
assumptions: Gas-to-dust ratio 100, locally isothermal disk with T proportional to R^-0.5 and surface density proportional to R^-1

recipe.goal: Radiative transfer of the SPH models and comparison with ALMA profiles
recipe.method: MCFOST Monte Carlo radiative transfer on the SPH Voronoi mesh, 1.3 and 3 mm images convolved with ALMA beams, radial profiles with GOFISH
key_parameters: Star: 5000 K black body, R = 1.25 Rsun, M = 1.3 Msun; N_gamma = 1e8 photons for temperature and for ray-tracing images
assumptions: DIANA dust: 60% silicates, 15% amorphous carbon, 25% porosity; local thermal equilibrium; passive stellar heating
